quote: we're talking to a son around and got a quote.
stewart_read: First mention of a competing quote; rep pivots straight to address confirmation instead of asking which company or what was shown.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be strategically deferring detail to the specialist call, but no bridge line ('the specialist will compare that design against ours') was ever made.
coaching_implication: Ask a follow-up question here: 'Who gave you that quote, and what did they show you?' — turns a passive fact into comparison ammo for the appointment.

quote: It's 38 solar panels is what's on our own dish.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers full existing design specs (panel count, battery count) — a gift-wrapped comparison hook the rep files instead of using.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be intentionally saving the comparison for the specialist rather than duplicating it himself, consistent with setter scope discipline.
coaching_implication: Even staying in scope, the rep should reflect the number back: 'Got it — 38 panels and battery backup, that's great context for our specialist to compare against.' Filing it silently wastes a strong anchor.

quote: My wife wouldn't wanna see them from the street.
stewart_read: Customer surfaces a spouse-driven aesthetic concern; rep responds with a design reassurance but never flags the wife as a co-decider who needs to be on the final call.
coaching_implication: This is also a spouse-inclusion cue — rep should have asked directly whether the wife would join the appointment.

quote: Looking at your roof, I do see I mean, you have a pretty great candidate.
stewart_read: Rep volunteers a roof-placement assessment (south-facing panel siting) before any specialist visit — accurate-but-premature content that belongs to the closer.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as rapport-building small talk rather than true scope creep since it's brief and non-technical.
coaching_implication: Redirect design-specific commentary to the specialist: 'Our specialist will map out exactly where they'd go so it fits what you and your wife want.'

quote: Is that not something we can do over the phone?
stewart_read: Customer pushes to convert the in-person visit to a phone call; rep accommodates but the appointment type flips mid-negotiation.
coaching_implication: When channel changes late, re-confirm all attendees (wife) for the new format explicitly rather than assuming the original arrangement carries over.

quote: I'll get you down for tomorrow then for a phone call.
stewart_read: Final booking lacks the 'is that fair?' handshake, no mention of one-hour block, no re-confirmation of the wife joining the call.
alternative_hypothesis: Customer's own line 'sounds good' at 10:20 could be read as an informal handshake substitute.
coaching_implication: Lock the appointment with the full button-up: confirm duration, no-driving/sit-down expectation, and explicitly ask if the wife will be on the call too.
